decisions.decision: The measured defect, re-read by the coordinator at 9a09ef8 rather than taken from V2-079's escalation, because it is one line doing two wrong things at once. internal/api/api.go:1116 domainError checks quota.ErrOverBudget first (429 quota_exhausted, api.go:1117-1126), then sets status := http.StatusBadRequest and code := "invalid_request" (api.go:1127-1128), then overrides that default for exactly eight sentinel groups -- application.ErrNotFound 404 not_found, application.ErrUnauthenticated 401 unauthorized, application.ErrForbidden 403 forbidden, domain.ErrControlDenied or domain.ErrLeaseNotOwned 403 policy_denied, domain.ErrStaleVersion 409 conflict, application.ErrRepositoryAlreadyRegistered 409 conflict, domain.ErrStaleFence or domain.ErrLeaseExpired or application.ErrIdempotencyConflict 409 conflict, application.ErrAwaitingHumanInput 409 conflict -- and finally calls h.error(w, r, status, code, err.Error()) at api.go:1168. Defect (a): anything not in that list of eight leaves as 400 invalid_request, so a fault the request did not cause is reported as the caller's mistake. Defect (b): whatever text the error carries is echoed to the caller verbatim, because h.error (api.go:1177) writes it as the response's message field. There are 24 call sites, measured: internal/api/api.go:94 (the /internal/reconcile branch) and 22 handler sites (renew :549, start :570, requestHumanInput :642, answerHumanInput :660, heartbeat :705, listRunners :720, listProviders :736, checkpoint :755, listRequirements :772, getRequirement :780, listControls :802, releaseState :825, queueSummary :834, export :860, capture :938, control :986, claim :1007, permit :1030, result :1081) plus internal/api/repositories.go:76, :89, :102, :111, :120. That is the whole authenticated surface, which is why this task is stated over every route and not over paging.
decisions.rationale: V2-079 reproduced the concrete case against the emulator: internal/store/firestore's paged read handed StartAfter a doubly-prefixed parent name, the server refused it with gRPC InvalidArgument, and the caller was told 400 invalid_request with the server's own message. The reason that read as a bad cursor for three exercises is not that the mapping lacked one entry; it is that the mapping's default asserts something it cannot know -- that an unrecognised error is the caller's fault. Every route inherits that assertion, so the repair has to be the default itself, and the cost of touching the default is that it can move a status code on any of 24 sites. That cost is what d6 exists to bound.

decisions.decision: The default becomes 500 with code internal_error and the fixed message "internal server error" -- byte-identical to the panic-recovery branch already in the same file (internal/api/api.go:49-53), which answers exactly that triple. Not 503 (that spelling is taken: not_configured, api.go's authenticated-API guard, and it means this process was never wired, not that a dependency failed), not 502 (this transport has no upstream it proxies), and not 429 (the only capacity answer is the quota branch, which stays first and untouched).
decisions.rationale: Three properties decide it. It is already the code this file uses for 'something failed and the caller cannot fix it', so the surface gains no new vocabulary and every existing client that handles 5xx handles this. It is honest about attribution, which is the outcome sentence. And it is retryable-by-nature in the way 400 is not: a caller that receives 400 will rewrite its request forever, which is precisely what happened for three exercises. Reusing the panic branch's exact code and message also means the two 500 paths in this file cannot drift apart, and one assertion covers both.

decisions.decision: The information-leak judgement, which the coordinator measured rather than assumed: today the message IS returned. h.error (internal/api/api.go:1177) writes {"error": code, "message": msg, "schema_version": "v1", "correlation_id": ...} and domainError passes err.Error() as msg (api.go:1168), so the pre-change tree returned the gRPC InvalidArgument text -- the doubled Firestore parent name carrying the installation key and the collection segments, plus a byte offset -- straight to the caller. Moving the status to 500 without also dropping the message would therefore fix the attribution and keep the disclosure. So the new default branch passes a CONSTANT message and never err.Error(). The eight already-classified branches keep err.Error(), so no existing response message changes by a single byte.
decisions.rationale: The precedent is in the same function and is explicit about this: the quota branch (api.go:1117-1126) deliberately answers with a fixed sentence and its comment says it 'never echoes the wrapped error's actual usage figures'. The new default is the same argument applied to a class that is strictly more sensitive, because an unclassified error is by definition one nobody vetted for what it carries -- it can be an adapter's resource path, a serialization failure quoting a payload, or a wrapped dependency's diagnostic. Keeping err.Error() on the classified branches is not laziness either: those eight sentinels are declared in internal/application and internal/domain, their texts are authored by this repository, and several existing tests read them. Changing them would be a second, unrelated behaviour change hiding inside this one.

decisions.decision: Classification material is sentinel identity through errors.Is, and nothing else. Not the dependency's text (non_goals item 1), not a type assertion on an adapter type, not a gRPC status code, and not the error's position in the call graph. domainError gains ONE new positive branch -- errors.Is(err, application.ErrInvalidRequest) -> 400 invalid_request -- plus an explicit, commented list of the already-exported sentinels that are caller faults and are not in the eight groups today, which internal/api may name directly because it already imports both internal/application and internal/domain (api.go:19-20). internal/domain is not edited at all.
decisions.rationale: Text matching is forbidden by the task and would be wrong anyway: the string that revealed this defect came from a Google client library and can change in a patch release, which is how a classifier built on text becomes a silent 400 again. Sentinel identity is the only material both layers already share -- errors.Is is what the existing eight branches use, so the new branches are the same idiom rather than a second one. The reason a NEW sentinel is needed on top of the existing exported ones is measured: the caller-fault errors reaching these routes are not all sentinels today. internal/application authors plain errors at validation sites (internal/application/service.go:24-29 requireRequest returns errors.New("request_id is required"); internal/application/readmodels.go:126, :358 and :450 return fmt.Errorf page_size and export-limit bounds), and those are 400 today and must stay 400. Naming internal/domain's sentinels from the api side rather than editing internal/domain is what keeps this task out of the domain component and its closure proof entirely.

decisions.decision: The caller-fault marker preserves the message exactly. internal/application gains one new file, internal/application/errors.go, holding the exported sentinel ErrInvalidRequest and an unexported constructor that wraps an authored validation error so that errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRequest) is true while Error() returns the ORIGINAL text unchanged -- a small struct with Error() delegating to the wrapped error, Unwrap() returning it, and Is(target) matching ErrInvalidRequest. It is NOT done by re-declaring existing sentinels as fmt.Errorf("%w: ...", ErrInvalidRequest) and NOT by fmt.Errorf("%w: request_id is required", ErrInvalidRequest) at each site.
decisions.rationale: Both rejected spellings prepend the sentinel's own text to every message, so 'request_id is required' becomes 'invalid request: request_id is required' on the wire. That is a response-body change on routes this task is not supposed to touch, it would move golden bodies and any test reading a message substring, and it would make the diff impossible to review for the one property that matters: that no observable behaviour moved except the default. A marker type that is transparent in Error() makes the change provably message-neutral, which is what lets d6's pin table be an equality assertion on both the code and the body rather than on the code alone.

decisions.decision: The wrap set is DISCOVERED BY MEASUREMENT, in this order, and the order is part of the design. (1) Write the route pin table -- one new table-driven test in internal/api/api_test.go covering every route the router reaches, each row naming method, path, role, body and the expected status and error code -- and run it GREEN ON THE UNEDITED TREE, recording the whole table in the evidence as the measured baseline. (2) Flip the default to 500 and change nothing else. (3) Every row that turns red is repaired ONLY by marking the caller-fault error at the site that authors it, never by re-adding a default, never by adding a route-specific special case in internal/api, and never by relaxing an assertion. (4) Re-run the pin table plus go test ./... and go vet ./..., because internal/application, internal/reconciler and internal/runner tests assert error identities that a wrap must not break.
decisions.rationale: This is the only way to satisfy 'change no existing status code' as a measurement rather than a hope, and it is the answer to the coordinator's question of how a change that touches every route proves it moved nothing. Guessing the wrap set from a grep of internal/application would be unsound in both directions: 118 non-test error constructions in internal/application and 77 in internal/domain were measured at 9a09ef8, most unreachable from any route, and several -- "clock returned zero time" at service.go:779 and allocation.go:564, the adapter's own "invalid requirement page limit" at internal/store/firestore/store.go:645 -- are faults the request did not cause and MUST be allowed to become 500. Writing the table first also means the baseline is recorded evidence rather than a claim, so a reviewer can see exactly which codes existed before the flip.

decisions.decision: V2-079's boundary is inherited verbatim and its test is the guard. TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue (internal/api/api_test.go, measured at 9a09ef8 as FIVE refused shapes -- fabricated-not-base64url, envelope-version-is-not-v1, truncated-prefix-of-a-real-cursor, another-collections-document-key-space, another-paged-reads-cursor-shape -- and TWO accepted shapes, a v1 envelope naming a Requirement that does not exist and one naming another aggregate's id) must keep its name, keep every assertion, stay byte-unchanged, and pass. The mechanism that makes that automatic rather than lucky: the refusals all arrive as application.ErrInvalidCursor (internal/application/readmodels.go:21, returned by decodeCursor at readmodels.go:35-51), which is an existing exported sentinel and therefore goes into d4's caller-fault list explicitly.
decisions.rationale: The task's own dependency is V2-079, and the reason the dependency exists is that its refusal tests are the fixture this change could most easily break: a default flip is exactly the change that turns a 400 into a 500 for a shape nobody re-classified. Note that the coordinator's brief said four refused shapes and the tree says five; the implementer re-measures and uses the tree. If that test needs any edit at all to pass, the design was departed from and the correct action is to stop and escalate, because the only reason it could need editing is that a caller fault stopped being classified as one.

decisions.decision: The repair is proved by injecting a fault at the store port, in a test-local Transactor decorator inside internal/api/api_test.go, in TWO variants that must both be asserted on every route that reaches domainError: (A) the decorator returns the fault INSTEAD of running the callback, and (B) the decorator runs the callback to completion and THEN returns the fault, which is the commit-time shape. For each route and each variant, assert: the status is 500, the code is internal_error, the status is NOT 400 and NOT any 2xx, the response body does not contain any part of the injected error's text, the body still carries exactly the four keys error, message, schema_version and correlation_id, and the X-Correlation-ID header is still set. The injected error is a plain errors.New carrying storage-shaped text (a doubled Firestore parent name with a byte offset, copied from V2-079's measurement); the test does NOT import a gRPC status package.
decisions.rationale: Variant B is what answers non_goals item 2: an unclassified failure must not become a success, and the only way a commit failure could be reported as 200 is if a handler ignored the transaction's error. Asserting it per route rather than once is what makes the claim 'on any route' true by measurement instead of by extrapolation from one handler. The absence-of-text assertion is how non_goals item 3 is checked: the test matches text to prove text is GONE, which is the opposite of classifying by text and is not what the non-goal forbids. A plain errors.New rather than a real gRPC status keeps the api component's import set unchanged, which matters because internal/ci derives the manifest from imports and a new edge would turn make check red for a reason unrelated to this repair.

decisions.decision: The class changes this task intends are enumerated up front and every one of them is unreachable through any pin-table row, which is why the table stays green: storage and adapter faults surfacing through the port (internal/store/firestore's gRPC errors, ErrInvalidSchema, ErrWriteCap, and the adapter's own "invalid requirement page limit"), "clock returned zero time" (internal/application/service.go:779, allocation.go:564, runner_version.go:297 and :321, provider_registry.go:742), context cancellation and deadline expiry, and a failure of the /internal/reconcile hook (internal/api/api.go:93, today a 400 for a reconciliation the caller did not perform). Each of these becomes 500. If any pin-table row moves, the design was departed from: stop and escalate rather than adjusting the row.
decisions.rationale: Naming the intended movement is the difference between a repair and a hope, and it is also the honest answer to 'does the caller lose anything'. Everything on this list is either impossible to trigger by a request at all (an injected zero clock, a decorator's fault) or is already not the caller's business (a reconcile hook failure). The two candidates that could look like caller faults were checked and left alone deliberately: domain.ErrInvalidTransition and application.ErrDuplicateRequest are 400 today and stay 400, even though a state-machine refusal arguably deserves 409, because moving them is a separate judgement about the API's vocabulary and this task's constraint is that no code moves.

decisions.decision: The application layer proves its half separately, in internal/application: a table-driven test asserting that every validation refusal reachable from a route satisfies errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRequest) -- capture with no request_id, a page_size below one and above application.MaxPageSize, an export limit out of range, and every other site the pin table proved reachable -- and, as the negative half, that a fault the request did not cause (a zero clock, a decorator's storage error) does NOT satisfy it. internal/domain gets no test change and no source change.
decisions.rationale: Without the negative half the marker would drift toward being applied everywhere, which would recreate the defect with a new spelling: a blanket ErrInvalidRequest wrap makes every 500 a 400 again. Asserting the class at the layer that authors the error also puts the assertion where a future author will see it, rather than only at the transport, and it is what makes the 400s survive later refactors of internal/api. Keeping internal/domain untouched is a deliberate chain decision as much as a design one: the domain component carries M1's closure proof and this task has no business near it.

decisions.decision: Two gaps are recorded and NOT fixed here. (a) contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is prohibited. Measured: four routes that call domainError declare neither '500' nor '400' -- GET /v1/requirements/{requirement_id} (openapi-v1.yaml:54), GET /v1/controls (:59), GET /v1/queue/summary (:69) and GET /v1/export (:127) -- while every other route already declares '500'. Nothing enforces response codes: internal/contracts/release_contract_test.go's openAPIDeclaredPaths (:324-332) extracts path KEYS only, and api_test.go's two openapi checks compare schema field lists. The 500 was already reachable on those four routes before this task through the panic-recovery branch, so the gap predates it. (b) No logging is added. Measured: NO non-test file under internal/ or cmd/ imports "log" or "log/slog" -- this repository has no logging idiom -- so once the default stops echoing err.Error() the dependency's own text is no longer visible anywhere in-process. The correlation id is still in the body and in the X-Correlation-ID header, and the fault remains reproducible against the emulator.
decisions.rationale: Editing openapi-v1.yaml would move the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest and would enrol this task in the api-contract chain that V2-082 already holds, for a declaration gap this change does not create. Introducing the repository's first logger at the transport boundary is a larger decision than an error-mapping repair -- where it writes, what it redacts, whether Cloud Run captures it -- and smuggling it in here would be the kind of scope creep that makes a small repair unreviewable. Both are written into the evidence as measured residuals with the follow-up named, because the honest cost of d3 is that a 500 now carries less information than the 400 it replaces, and a reader deserves to see that stated rather than discovered.

decisions.decision: Chain position, stated for the coordinator. Components: api and application. This task must be serialized AFTER V2-082, which holds internal/api/api.go and internal/api/api_test.go (measured from wo-v2-082's allowed_paths), and BEFORE V2-087, which holds internal/api/api_test.go for its quota-fill seam. V2-080 depends on both and is the live re-observation that must follow every source change. This task creates and removes no import edge: internal/api gains no import (it already imports internal/application and internal/domain) and internal/application gains one file that imports only errors and fmt.
decisions.rationale: Three tasks want internal/api/api_test.go and two want internal/api/api.go, so the only question is order, and this one goes in the middle for a measured reason: V2-082 adds a route, and a route added after the pin table exists must be added to the table, which is friction the wrong way round; V2-087 changes what the memory adapter charges for a reservation, and the pin table -- which contains the 429 quota row -- is exactly the guard that catches it if that change accidentally turns a 429 into a 201. Since ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are all prohibited and no edge moves, a red manifest or dependency-coverage check means the design was departed from.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api
risks: The pin table is the whole safety argument, and a table that is written after the flip proves nothing. If the implementer writes it against the already-changed tree, or edits a row to match a new answer, the task has silently become 'move whatever moved'. The baseline table must be recorded in the evidence with the argv that produced it, on the unedited tree, before internal/api/api.go is touched.

The wrap set can be over-applied. A blanket ErrInvalidRequest wrap at a shared helper -- or at Service.mutate, or around a transaction -- would drag storage faults back into 400 and recreate the defect behind a new spelling. Every wrap sits at the site that AUTHORS the validation error, and d10's negative assertions are what catch a wrap that climbed too high.

d5's message-transparent marker is easy to get subtly wrong: an Is method that matches too much, an Unwrap that hides the original, or a wrap applied to an error that already carries a sentinel could change which branch of domainError wins and move a 409 or a 404 to 400. The pin table covers every route's classified codes for exactly this reason, and the four-key body assertion catches a message that changed shape.

Losing err.Error() from the default makes a 500 less informative than the 400 it replaces, in a repository with no logging at all. That is an accepted cost (d11b), not an oversight, and the follow-up is named. An implementer who resolves the discomfort by putting the storage text back -- in the message, in a new field, or in a header -- has violated non_goals item 3.

internal/api/api.go and internal/api/api_test.go are held by V2-082, which is queued. Running the two concurrently conflicts in both files. Serialize V2-083 after V2-082, and add any route V2-082 introduced to the pin table as part of the baseline measurement rather than treating its absence as a table that is already complete.

The 429 quota row in the pin table depends on the in-memory adapter's current reservation behaviour, which V2-087 changes on purpose. That is the intended interaction and the reason for the ordering in d12: the row must be present and passing here so that V2-087 cannot move it unnoticed.
